narratives.Overview:
## Parent

#3613

## Recut (post-bind, 2026-09-05)

Operator recut after accepted synthesis [5555695949](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/4200#issuecomment-5555695949) / successor lean [5545894034](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/4200#issuecomment-5545894034).

Locked v1: a list-visible GitHub tag (label) plus a `task` / `deft` verb. That is the cheapest shape that meets the need.

Dropped from v1: required path/glob list, repo-wide path index, and two-issue path-overlap as an acceptance clause. Labels cannot carry paths. The first-arc blocking finding (issue-thread lookup cannot see two-issue path collision) is closed by dropping that job, not by adding an index.

The older completed-arc record does not clear this recut body.

## Problem

Occupancy answers who owns this checkout on this disk. An active xBRIEF answers that a story is in lifecycle, but only after a commit and a PR. That is the wrong tax for a coordination signal.

Two agents, often the same GitHub login, can start the same issue with no forge-visible warning. #3607 does not fill that hole: it marks a structured pass (triage / design-critique / review-response), it is advisory, it has no CLI verb, and we do not use it as "this issue is being implemented."

## Presumption (refutation target)

A list-visible GitHub label on the issue, written and listed by a `task` / `deft` verb, is the right cheap substitute for committing an active xBRIEF as the cross-machine "this issue is being worked" signal.

The useful job in v1 is same-issue double-start, not permission and not two-issue file collision. A flag on the issue says the issue is busy. A second agent who opened that issue can see the tag on the label list without reading comments.

## Proposed shape

GitHub label plus verb. Not a sticky HTML comment. Not `kind: pass`.

- One list-visible tag meaning this issue is being worked. Exact name is an open fork (`status:claimed` vs a new catalog name). Do not invent the label in the field before the catalog lands.
- Verb surface that claims, shows, and releases the tag (`task` / `deft`, names remaining). HTML-block-by-hand is not an on-ramp. Session-start / pre-edit may call show; the verb still exists.
- Read on arrival of that issue. If the tag is present, warn. Do not exclusive-lock the issue (parent + worker; forge-only sessions must not claim -- #4020).
- Clear on explicit release, and on PR-open / `scope:complete` when those events exist. Abandoned claims must not rot. Expiry over heartbeat if a timestamp is added later; v1 may be tag-only.
- Cooperative, like occupancy. Not authentication. #2307 maintainer-only would lock out CONTRIBUTOR cloud workers.
- Do not require xBRIEF promotion. A later brief may still declare `file_scope`; that is the heavier cousin, not the on-ramp.
- Last-write-wins on the label is accepted in v1. Do not inherit the review-owner comment writer (#3885 CAS / #3994 shared-login overwrite). Labels do not carry `agent_id`.

## Inventory (do not reinvent)

| Existing | Job | Why it is not this |
|---|---|---|
| Occupancy #3433 | Tree lock, local gitignored JSON | Single-machine by construction |
| #3607 kind: pass | Advisory pass-open on the issue thread | Pass, not implementation; unused in practice; blocking refuted; no verb |
| Sticky comment + path list (pre-recut body) | Intended two-issue path collision | Recut away: comments on issue A are invisible from issue B; labels cannot carry paths |
| PR review-owner lease #2814 | Fail-closed babysit owner | PR-anchored, after the PR exists |
| xBRIEF file_scope + #3145 | Provenance once a brief is approved | Requires lifecycle paper |
| #1379 | Multi-machine cache/audit sync | Not a work claim |
| #3885 / #3994 | Pass-marker RMW / shared-login overwrite | Do not reuse that comment writer |

## Non-goals

- A hard exclusive lock on the issue thread (#3607 already refused that for passes).
- Making occupancy cross-machine.
- A required path/glob list, or a repo-wide path index, in v1.
- Treating two-issue file collision as an acceptance clause in v1.
- Treating this as ingest clearance or as a substitute for file_scope after a brief exists.
- Hanging the signal on scope:promote / a lifecycle PR.

## Acceptance (draft)

- [ ] An agent can claim and release with GitHub writes only, through the verb (no tree mutation, no brief promote).
- [ ] A second agent opening the same issue can see the tag on the label list without reading the comment thread.
- [ ] Occupancy, #3607 pass marks, and PR review-owner leases remain separate kinds.
- [ ] Docs state collision vs permission, and that v1 does not detect two-issue path overlap.
- [ ] Content-contract / label catalog names the tag; agents do not invent it per issue.

## Open forks

- Exact label name (reuse `status:*` vs a new catalog name).
- Warn-only vs louder session-start halt when the tag is already present (still not an exclusive GitHub lock).
- Exact verb names (claim / show / release, or one verb with subcommands).
- Whether clear-on-PR-open / scope:complete is automatic in v1 or only explicit release.

Refs #3613, #3433, #3607, #3885, #3994, #4020, #3145, #1379, #2814, #4205.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-09-04T20:08:44Z)

model: grok-4.6
role: critic

Dispatch SHA: `a1fb975090234dcb3643c99dd43bd0504bc68194`
Ceiling: 5545822277. Charter: refutation.

Verdict on the refutation target: **not refuted as a hole**. Occupancy is local, #3607 is a pass mark, xBRIEF promote is the wrong tax. The cheap forge-visible signal is a real missing surface. The recorded **index** cannot carry the job the filing names.

## `blocks-the-design` — Issue-thread lookup cannot see two-issue path collision

Evidence. The operator problem, restated in the body and the Stop 1 write-back, is two machines (often one GitHub login) picking **two issues** and colliding on files. The proposed store is a sticky comment **on the issue being worked**. Arrival protocol in the body is "read on arrival" of that thread. An agent who opened #B never fetches #A's comments.

At the dispatch SHA, `openPassMarker` / `fetchActivePassMarker` live in `packages/core/src/review-monitor/github-lease.ts` and take a **single issue number**. There is no repo-wide claim index. GitHub issue comments are not a path index.

Concrete failure mode. Agent 1 claims #4200 with `packages/core/src/session/**`. Agent 2 starts #3884, reads #3884, sees no mark, edits the same files. The path list never fires. The lean's "useful job" is collision across issues; the store only reports collision on the same issue, which is the rare case.

Disposition consequence. Either (a) the lookup is repo-wide (search, a well-known tracker comment, or a label-plus-body census) before any edit, with an acceptance clause that names that scan, or (b) drop path-overlap-across-issues from the job and keep only "this issue already has a worker." As written, AC "a second agent on another machine can read live claims and see path overlap" is unsatisfiable.

## `sharpens-framing` — A comment protocol with no verb repeats #3607 non-use

Evidence. Stop 1 already records that #3607 shipped `kind: pass` with no `task` verb, that the design-critique skill does not mention it, and that #3873 / #4085 did not post it. At this SHA, `git grep openPassMarker` / `fetchActivePassMarker` under `tasks/` and `packages/cli/` is empty. The library exists; the operator surface does not.

Concrete failure mode. Agents will not post or scan a new HTML block by hand, for the same reason they do not post `kind: pass`. The feature can land in github-lease.ts and still be invisible in the field.

Disposition consequence. The lean must include a `task` (or `deft`) verb that writes and lists claims, or an always-on session-start / pre-edit scan. "Post a comment" is not an on-ramp.

## `sharpens-framing` — Reusing the review-owner comment inherits #3885 / #3994

Evidence. The body inventories those issues. `openPassMarker` updates a single issue comment. Comments have no compare-and-swap. `agentId` is optional on the pass-marker input at this SHA.

Concrete failure mode. Two shared-login agents omit agent_id, refresh the same kind, overwrite ceiling/paths. Or two renewals RMW-erase one path list. The collision board then lies.

Disposition consequence. New kind does not dodge this. Append-only claims, or require agent_id, or accept that the board is best-effort and write that into AC. Do not silently inherit the pass-marker writer.

## Injection / swarm lens

A forge-visible path list is untrusted input. If overlap is fail-closed, a CONTRIBUTOR can claim `**` and stall peers (the #3866-class commenter DoS). If overlap is warn-only, the signal is ignorable and we are back to #3607. Bound the glob language; refuse unbounded `**` if the verdict is fail-closed.

## Road not taken

Exclusive issue lock — already refused on #3607; the filing agrees. Occupancy-over-network — different machine, different disk; would not see the other worktree anyway.

## Steelman

Steelman for "same-issue comment is enough": most fights are two agents on the **same** ticket, and a thread mark is the cheapest GitHub write. That would flip the blocking finding only if the operator problem is restated as same-issue double-start, not two-issue path overlap. The body and Stop 1 both name the two-issue case.
